title: POCSAG: pages at 512 / 1200 / 2400 bit/s + an FM interferer
description: One paging transmitter (60 deg) sends a numeric (F0) and an alphanumeric (F3) page at each of 512, 1200 and 2400 bit/s; an analog FM transmitter (200 deg) talks in the gaps. POCSAG names no transmitter (the RIC is the pager being called, and networks simulcast), so there are no talkers: the check is the six decoded pages and the VFO's own DoA with the Digital squelch on - it is taken from the decoded batches only, so it stays on the pager's 60 deg and never shows the FM interferer.

expect.event: POCSAG 512 bit/s RIC 0400003 F3 alpha: TEST PAGE 512 BAUD
POCSAG 1200 bit/s RIC 0012345 F3 alpha: 1200 BAUD ALPHA PAGE
POCSAG 2400 bit/s RIC 0003456 F3 alpha: 2400 BIT/S MESSAGE

title: FLEX: frames at 1600 / 3200 / 6400 bit/s, 2- and 4-level
description: One FLEX transmitter (120 deg) sends six frames back to back, as FLEX systems do: 1600/2, 3200/2, 3200/4 and three at 6400/4 - alphanumeric and numeric pages to short and long capcodes, a tone-only page, a 3-digit short message, a binary page, an alphanumeric message in two fragments (put together), a group call (two pagers told to listen to a temporary address, then the message to it) and the date / time block information words. FLEX names no transmitter either (the capcode is the pager called; networks simulcast): the check is the decoded pages and the VFO's own DoA with the Digital squelch, taken from the decoded blocks only.
steps: FRAGMENT ONE OF A LONG ONE, |AND FRAGMENT TWO.

expect.event: FLEX 1600/2 capcode 1234567 alpha: FLEX 1600 BIT/S ALPHANUMERIC PAGE
FLEX 3200/2 capcode 002345678 alpha: LONG ADDRESS AT 3200/2
FLEX 6400/4 capcode 1000000 alpha: FRAGMENT ONE OF A LONG ONE, AND FRAGMENT TWO.
(to 2 pagers: 1000008 1000012) alpha: MESSAGE TO THE GROUP
